question: The Pharmacy (Amendment) Bill, 2023 was introduced in Lok Sabha on 3 August 2023, which amends the ____________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pharmacy Act, 1948.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Pharmacy (Amendment) Bill, 2023, introduced in the Lok Sabha on 3 August 2023, amends the Pharmacy Act, 1948. (फार्मेसी अधिनियम, 1948)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Pharmacy Act, 1948 regulates the profession and practice of pharmacy in India and provides for the constitution of the Pharmacy Council of India (PCI) and State Pharmacy Councils.

• The 2023 amendment provided that persons registered under the Jammu and Kashmir Pharmacy Act, 2011 (or with prescribed qualifications) shall be deemed registered under the Pharmacy Act, 1948.

NOTE

• Other important health laws: Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940; Indian Medical Council Act, 1956 (replaced by the National Medical Commission Act, 2019).

question: In which state/union territory is Losar celebrated to mark the start of the new year in that region?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ladakh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Losar" is the Tibetan/Buddhist New Year festival celebrated in the Union Territory of Ladakh (and other Himalayan Buddhist regions) to mark the beginning of the new year. (लोसर — लद्दाख का नववर्ष पर्व)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Losar celebrations include prayers in monasteries (gompas), folk dances, music, the lighting of lamps and family feasts.

• Other festivals of Ladakh: Hemis Festival (birth anniversary of Guru Padmasambhava), Ladakh Harvest Festival and Sindhu Darshan.

• Ladakh became a Union Territory on 31 October 2019 after the reorganisation of Jammu and Kashmir.

NOTE

• Regional New Year festivals of India: Ugadi (Andhra Pradesh/Karnataka), Gudi Padwa (Maharashtra), Vishu (Kerala), Baisakhi (Punjab), Bohag/Rongali Bihu (Assam), Navreh (Kashmir), Losar (Ladakh/Buddhists).

question: Kanak Rele, who established Nalanda Dance Research Centre, was a performer of which of the following classical dance forms of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mohiniyattam.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Dr. Kanak Rele, who founded the Nalanda Dance Research Centre (1966) and the Nalanda Nritya Kala Mahavidyalaya, Mumbai, was a celebrated exponent of "Mohiniyattam". (कनक रेले — मोहिनीअट्टम)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Mohiniyattam is the classical dance form of Kerala, performed traditionally by women; the name means "dance of Mohini", the female enchantress avatar of Lord Vishnu.

• Kanak Rele received the Padma Shri (1990), the Padma Bhushan (2013) and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award; she pioneered the academic study of Mohiniyattam.

NOTE

• The eight classical dances of India: Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (North India), Kathakali and Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur), Sattriya (Assam).

question: Which of the following acts introduced the system of dyarchy in the provincial administration in India?
option_1: The Government of India Act of 1909
option_2: The Government of India Act of 1919
option_3: The Government of India Act of 1935
option_4: The Government of India Act of 1947
solution_text:
The correct answer is The Government of India Act of 1919.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Government of India Act, 1919 (also called the Montagu–Chelmsford Reforms) introduced "dyarchy" (double government) in the provinces: provincial subjects were divided into Transferred subjects (administered by the Governor with ministers responsible to the legislative council) and Reserved subjects (administered by the Governor and his executive council). (द्वैध शासन — 1919 का अधिनियम)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Act also introduced bicameralism at the Centre (Council of State and Legislative Assembly) and extended communal representation.

• The Act of 1909 (Morley–Minto Reforms) introduced separate electorates for Muslims.

• The Act of 1935 abolished dyarchy in the provinces, introduced provincial autonomy, and proposed dyarchy at the Centre (never implemented).

NOTE

• The word "dyarchy" comes from the Greek "di-arche" meaning double rule. Dyarchy in provinces operated from 1921 to 1937.

question: In which part of India is cool mountain climate observed?
solution_text:
The correct answer is North.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The cool mountain (highland) climate is observed in the northern part of India, in the Himalayan region — Jammu & Kashmir, Ladakh, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Sikkim and Arunachal Pradesh — where altitude keeps temperatures low. (शीतल पर्वतीय जलवायु — उत्तर भारत)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• In mountains, temperature decreases with height at about 6.5°C per 1,000 m (the normal lapse rate), producing a cool climate even in summer.

• India's overall climate is tropical monsoon type; the Himalayas act as a climatic barrier blocking cold Central Asian winds and forcing monsoon winds to shed rain.

NOTE

• Broad climatic regions of India: tropical wet (west coast/northeast), tropical dry/steppe (interior peninsula), desert (Rajasthan), sub-tropical humid (northern plains) and mountain/alpine climate (Himalayas).

question: Who was the founder of the Mauryan dynasty?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chandragupta Maurya.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Chandragupta Maurya founded the Mauryan dynasty/empire in 322/321 BCE by overthrowing the last Nanda ruler Dhana Nanda, with the guidance of Chanakya (Kautilya/Vishnugupta). The capital was Pataliputra. (चंद्रगुप्त मौर्य — मौर्य वंश के संस्थापक)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Bindusara (his son) succeeded him, followed by Ashoka the Great, under whom the empire reached its zenith; Ashoka embraced Buddhism after the Kalinga War (261 BCE).

• Chandragupta defeated Seleucus Nicator (c. 305 BCE); Seleucus's ambassador Megasthenes wrote the "Indica". Kautilya wrote the "Arthashastra" (treatise on statecraft).

• In his last years Chandragupta embraced Jainism and, with the monk Bhadrabahu, migrated to Shravanabelagola (Karnataka).

NOTE

• "Vikramaditya" is a title associated with later rulers (e.g., Chandragupta II of the Gupta dynasty). The last Mauryan ruler, Brihadratha, was killed by Pushyamitra Shunga (c. 185 BCE).

question: As of 31st October 2023, the senior-most member (in terms of age) in the 17th Lok Sabha, Shafiqur Rahman Barq represents which political party?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Samajwadi Party.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Shafiqur Rahman Barq, the senior-most (oldest) member of the 17th Lok Sabha, represented the "Samajwadi Party (SP)" from the Sambhal constituency of Uttar Pradesh. (शफीकुर रहमान बर्क — समाजवादी पार्टी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Samajwadi Party was founded by Mulayam Singh Yadav in 1992; its symbol is the bicycle and its base is Uttar Pradesh.

• The youngest MP of the 17th Lok Sabha was Chandrani Murmu (Biju Janata Dal, Keonjhar, Odisha).

• The 17th Lok Sabha was constituted after the 2019 General Elections; its Speaker was Om Birla.

NOTE

• Eligibility for Lok Sabha membership (Article 84): citizen of India, minimum age 25 years; for Rajya Sabha, 30 years. There is no upper age limit for MPs.

question: Which of the following books is written by Dadabhai Naoroji?
option_3: Poverty and Un-British Rule in India
solution_text:
The correct answer is Poverty and Un-British Rule in India.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Poverty and Un-British Rule in India" (1901) was written by Dadabhai Naoroji. In it he propounded the famous "Drain of Wealth" theory — that Britain was draining India's wealth and causing its poverty. (दादाभाई नौरोजी — धन-निष्कासन सिद्धांत)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Dadabhai Naoroji is called the "Grand Old Man of India"; he was thrice President of the Indian National Congress (1886, 1893, 1906) and, at the 1906 Calcutta session, first used the word "Swaraj" from the Congress platform.

• He was the first Indian to be elected to the British House of Commons (1892, Liberal Party, Finsbury Central).

NOTE

• Other early economic critiques: R. C. Dutt's "The Economic History of India", which also exposed colonial exploitation. The drain theory became a key ideological weapon of the moderate nationalists.

question: The historical fiction ‘The Glory of Patan’ by KM Munshi was originally written in which Indian language?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gujarati.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "The Glory of Patan" is the English translation of "Patan-ni-Prabhuta" (1916), a historical novel originally written in "Gujarati" by Kanaiyalal Maneklal (K. M.) Munshi. It is set in the Patan of the Solanki (Chaulukya) dynasty of Gujarat. (के. एम. मुंशी — गुजराती)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• K. M. Munshi founded the "Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan" (1938), was a member of the Constituent Assembly, and served as Governor of Uttar Pradesh.

• His Patan trilogy: Patan-ni-Prabhuta, Gujarat-no-Nath and Rajadhiraj.

• He played a key role in the reconstruction of the Somnath temple.

NOTE

• Patan (Anhilwara) in Gujarat was the capital of the Solanki dynasty and is famous for the UNESCO World Heritage stepwell "Rani-ki-Vav" (built by Queen Udayamati).

question: On which date did Punjab abolish the Legislative Council?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1 January 1970.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Punjab abolished its Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad) on 1 January 1970, becoming a unicameral state with only a Legislative Assembly. (पंजाब विधान परिषद — 1 जनवरी 1970 को समाप्त)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Under Article 169, Parliament can create or abolish a State Legislative Council if the State Assembly passes a resolution by a special majority (majority of total membership and two-thirds of members present and voting).

• Currently only six states have Legislative Councils: Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.

• Provisions relating to Councils: Article 171 (composition — its size cannot exceed one-third of the Assembly's strength, minimum 40 members).

NOTE

• A Legislative Council is a permanent body (not subject to dissolution); one-third of its members retire every two years, and members serve six-year terms.

question: The chemical compound present in turmeric is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is curcumin.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Curcumin" is the natural yellow pigment/compound present in turmeric (Curcuma longa). It gives turmeric its colour and medicinal (antiseptic, anti-inflammatory) properties. (हल्दी — करक्यूमिन)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Curcumin is also used as a natural indicator — turmeric turns reddish-brown in bases (e.g., soap solution).

• Tartaric acid is found in tamarind and grapes; carotene is the orange pigment in carrots (a precursor of Vitamin A); capsaicin causes the pungency (hotness) of chillies.

NOTE

• Common natural compounds asked in SSC: tomato — lycopene; carrot — carotene; chilli — capsaicin; turmeric — curcumin; vinegar — acetic acid; lemon/orange — citric acid; apple — malic acid; milk — lactic acid.

question: Who among the following established the Indore gharana?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ustad Amir Khan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Indore gharana" of Hindustani classical (khayal) vocal music was established by Ustad Amir Khan (1912–1974). His style blended elements of the Kirana, Bhendibazaar and Jaipur styles with a meditative, slow (vilambit) elaboration. (इंदौर घराना — उस्ताद आमिर ख़ान)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Pt. Bhimsen Joshi belonged to the Kirana gharana (founded by Ustad Abdul Karim Khan); he received the Bharat Ratna in 2008.

• Tansen, one of the "Navaratnas" of Akbar's court, is regarded as the fountainhead of the Gwalior tradition of Hindustani music.

• Ustad Ghaghe Khuda Baksh is regarded as the founder of the Agra gharana.

NOTE

• Major khayal gharanas: Gwalior (oldest), Agra, Kirana, Jaipur-Atrauli, Patiala, Bhendibazaar, Indore, Rampur-Sahaswan. A "gharana" denotes a lineage/school with a distinct style of performance.

question: With reference to medieval Indian architecture style, what is ‘Pietra Dura’?
option_1: Sculpture art of the Mauryan period
option_2: Oil paintings on the walls of Taj Mahal
option_3: Fine quality clothes used by the Mughals
option_4: Decorating the walls with floral designs made of semi-precious stones
solution_text:
The correct answer is Decorating the walls with floral designs made of semi-precious stones.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Pietra Dura" (Italian for "hard stone"; known in India as parchin kari) is the technique of inlaying walls with floral and geometrical designs made of semi-precious stones (jade, jasper, carnelian, lapis lazuli, onyx) set into marble. (पित्रा दुरा — अर्ध-कीमती पत्थरों की पच्चीकारी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Pietra dura reached its height under the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan — it is seen splendidly on the Taj Mahal, Agra, and in the Diwan-i-Khas of the Red Fort.

• The technique first appeared prominently in the tomb of Itimad-ud-Daulah, Agra (built by Nur Jahan for her father), often called the "Baby Taj".

NOTE

• Other Mughal architectural features: charbagh (four-quartered garden), pietra dura inlay, bulbous domes, jali (lattice) screens, chhatris and minarets. The Taj Mahal was built by Shah Jahan in memory of Mumtaz Mahal (completed c. 1648).

question: The Rabi season of agriculture begins in October-November and ends in __________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is March-April.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Rabi" (winter) cropping season begins with sowing in October–November and ends with harvesting in March–April. (रबी — बुवाई अक्टूबर-नवंबर, कटाई मार्च-अप्रैल)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Major Rabi crops: wheat, barley, gram, peas, mustard, linseed.

• Kharif crops are sown with the onset of the monsoon (June–July) and harvested in September–October — rice, maize, jowar, bajra, cotton, groundnut, soybean.

• Zaid is the short summer season (March–June) — watermelon, muskmelon, cucumber, fodder crops.

NOTE

• "Rabi" (Arabic: spring) crops are harvested in spring; "Kharif" (Arabic: autumn) crops are harvested in autumn. Winter rainfall from western disturbances benefits the Rabi (wheat) crop in north-west India.

question: What is the chemical formula for sodium bicarbonate?
solution_text:
The correct answer is NaHCO3.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The chemical formula of sodium bicarbonate (sodium hydrogen carbonate) is "NaHCO₃". It is commonly called "baking soda" (खाने का सोडा / बेकिंग सोडा).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• NaCl — sodium chloride (common salt); Na₂CO₃ — sodium carbonate (washing soda, hydrated form Na₂CO₃·10H₂O); NaOH — sodium hydroxide (caustic soda).

• Baking soda is a mild base; it is used in baking (releases CO₂ making cakes fluffy), in antacids (neutralises stomach acid) and in soda-acid fire extinguishers.

• It is prepared by the Solvay process: NaCl + H₂O + CO₂ + NH₃ → NH₄Cl + NaHCO₃.

NOTE

• Common compound names: baking soda — NaHCO₃; washing soda — Na₂CO₃·10H₂O; caustic soda — NaOH; bleaching powder — CaOCl₂; plaster of Paris — CaSO₄·½H₂O; gypsum — CaSO₄·2H₂O.

question: Which of the following is one of the features of capital goods?
solution_text:
The correct answer is They are durable.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Capital goods" are goods used in the production of other goods and services — machines, plant, equipment, tools, buildings. A key feature is that they are "durable": they do not get used up in a single act of production and are used repeatedly over years. (पूंजीगत वस्तुएँ — टिकाऊ)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Capital goods are generally expensive (not inexpensive) and undergo depreciation (wear and tear) over time.

• Giffen goods are special inferior goods whose demand rises when their price rises (paradox of demand); inferior goods are goods whose demand falls as income rises — neither describes capital goods.

• Final goods are of two types: consumer goods (directly satisfy wants) and capital goods (used for further production).

NOTE

• Investment in capital goods is called gross capital formation and is vital for economic growth. Depreciation = consumption of fixed capital; Net investment = Gross investment − Depreciation.

question: निम्न से कौन-सा पद्म पुरस्कारों का घटता क्रम क्या है?
option_1: पद्म श्री, पद्म विभूषण, पद्म भूषण
option_2: पद्म भूषण, पद्म श्री, पद्म विभूषण
option_3: पद्म विभूषण, पद्म भूषण, पद्म श्री
option_4: पद्म श्री, पद्म भूषण, पद्म विभूषण
solution_text:
The correct answer is पद्म विभूषण, पद्म भूषण, पद्म श्री.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The decreasing (descending) order of the Padma awards is: "Padma Vibhushan → Padma Bhushan → Padma Shri" (पद्म विभूषण > पद्म भूषण > पद्म श्री).

◦ Padma Vibhushan — for exceptional and distinguished service (दूसरा सर्वोच्च नागरिक सम्मान).

◦ Padma Bhushan — for distinguished service of a high order.

◦ Padma Shri — for distinguished service in any field.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Bharat Ratna is India's highest civilian award; the Padma awards rank below it.

• The Padma awards were instituted in 1954 and are announced every year on Republic Day (26 January); they are conferred by the President of India.

• The awards were briefly suspended (1978–79 and 1993–97).

NOTE

• Civilian honours in decreasing order: Bharat Ratna > Padma Vibhushan > Padma Bhushan > Padma Shri. The awards are not titles under Article 18 and cannot be used as prefixes/suffixes to names.

question: Which of the following dynasties established the Vijayanagara kingdom in fourteenth century?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sangama dynasty.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Vijayanagara kingdom was founded in 1336 CE by the brothers Harihara I and Bukka Raya I of the "Sangama dynasty", with the blessings of the sage Vidyaranya. Its capital was Vijayanagara (Hampi) on the banks of the Tungabhadra river. (संगम वंश — 1336, हरिहर और बुक्का)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Four dynasties ruled Vijayanagara in order: Sangama (1336–1485) → Saluva (1485–1505) → Tuluva (1505–1570) → Aravidu (1570–1650).

• The greatest ruler, Krishnadevaraya (1509–1529) of the Tuluva dynasty, wrote "Amuktamalyada" (in Telugu) and was titled "Andhra Bhoja".

• The empire declined after the Battle of Talikota (1565) against the combined Deccan Sultanates.

NOTE

• Hampi is a UNESCO World Heritage Site (Virupaksha temple, Vittala temple with its stone chariot). Foreign travellers who visited Vijayanagara: Nicolo Conti, Abdur Razzaq, Domingo Paes, Fernao Nuniz.

question: The red colour of tomatoes is due to the presence of:
solution_text:
The correct answer is lycopene.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The red colour of tomatoes is due to "lycopene", a red carotenoid pigment and a powerful antioxidant. (टमाटर का लाल रंग — लाइकोपीन)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Lycopene is also responsible for the red/pink colour of watermelon, papaya and pink grapefruit; it is linked with reduced risk of certain cancers and heart disease.

• Limonene gives citrus fruits (lemon/orange peel) their smell; beta carotene is the orange pigment of carrots (converted into Vitamin A in the body); alizarin is a red dye obtained historically from the madder plant.

NOTE

• Pigments to remember: tomato — lycopene; carrot — carotene; turmeric — curcumin; chilli — capsaicin; leaves — chlorophyll (green); beetroot — betanin.

question: Which Union Territory had minimum literacy rate as per 2011 Census?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dadra and Nagar Haveli.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the Census of India 2011, among the given Union Territories, "Dadra and Nagar Haveli" had the minimum literacy rate — about 76.24%. (दादरा और नगर हवेली — न्यूनतम साक्षरता दर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Literacy rates (2011): Lakshadweep — 91.85% (highest among UTs), Chandigarh — 86.05%, Delhi — 86.21%, Dadra and Nagar Haveli — 76.24%.

• India's overall literacy rate (2011): 74.04% (males 82.14%, females 65.46%). Kerala had the highest state literacy (94%), Bihar the lowest (61.8%).

• In 2020, Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu were merged into a single Union Territory.

NOTE

• Census 2011 was the 15th Census of India (7th after Independence); its motto was "Our Census, Our Future". Literacy rate is calculated for the population aged 7 years and above.

question: In 1976, in which Part of the Indian Constitution under Article 51A were Fundamental Duties added?
solution_text:
The correct answer is IV A.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Fundamental Duties were added to the Constitution by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976, in a new "Part IV-A" containing a single article — "Article 51A". (मौलिक कर्तव्य — भाग IV-A, अनुच्छेद 51A)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• They were added on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee and were inspired by the Constitution of the erstwhile USSR.

• Originally 10 duties; the 11th duty (parents/guardians to provide education to children aged 6–14) was added by the 86th Amendment Act, 2002.

• Fundamental Duties apply only to citizens and are non-justiciable (not enforceable by courts).

NOTE

• Parts of the Constitution: Part III — Fundamental Rights; Part IV — Directive Principles of State Policy; Part IV-A — Fundamental Duties; Part V — the Union; Part VI — the States.

question: With which sport is Sanjana Bathula associated?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Roller skating.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sanjana Bathula is a young Indian sportsperson associated with "roller skating". The Hyderabad-based skater has won medals for India in international roller-skating events. (संजना बथुला — रोलर स्केटिंग)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• India won medals in roller skating (skateboarding/speed skating events) at the Asian Games 2022 (Hangzhou), where the sport gained wide attention.

• Roller sports are governed internationally by World Skate and in India by the Roller Skating Federation of India (RSFI).

NOTE

• Sports–personality matching is a routine SSC question type; remember: squash — Joshna Chinappa, Saurav Ghosal; shooting — Manu Bhaker, Abhinav Bindra; badminton — P. V. Sindhu, Saina Nehwal.

question: Who was the captain of Royal Challengers Bangalore in the Women's Premier League event 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Smriti Mandhana.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Smriti Mandhana was the captain of Royal Challengers Bangalore (RCB) in the inaugural Women's Premier League (WPL) 2023. She was also the costliest player of the first WPL auction (₹3.4 crore). (स्मृति मंधाना — आरसीबी कप्तान)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The first WPL title (2023) was won by Mumbai Indians, captained by Harmanpreet Kaur; Delhi Capitals (captain Meg Lanning) were runners-up.

• The WPL 2023 had five teams: Mumbai Indians, Delhi Capitals, Royal Challengers Bangalore, UP Warriorz and Gujarat Giants.

• In WPL 2024, RCB under Smriti Mandhana won the title.

NOTE

• Smriti Mandhana has won the ICC Women's Cricketer of the Year (Rachael Heyhoe Flint Trophy) and is a leading opener of the Indian women's team; Shafali Verma and Deepti Sharma played for Delhi Capitals and UP Warriorz respectively in WPL 2023.

question:
Which of the following statements is/are correct about the famous place Mawsynram?

A. It is the wettest place on the earth.

B. It is located in Meghalaya state of India.
option_2: Neither A nor B is correct.
option_4: A and B both are correct.
solution_text:
The correct answer is A and B both are correct.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Statement A is correct: "Mawsynram" is regarded as the wettest place on the Earth, receiving the highest average annual rainfall in the world (about 11,872 mm).

• Statement B is correct: Mawsynram is located in the East Khasi Hills district of Meghalaya, India. (मौसिनराम — मेघालय, विश्व का सबसे आर्द्र स्थान)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Nearby Cherrapunji (Sohra), also in Meghalaya, was earlier considered the wettest place and still holds several single-year rainfall records.

• The exceptional rain is caused by the funnelling of moist Bay of Bengal monsoon winds against the Khasi Hills, forcing them to rise (orographic rainfall).

• "Meghalaya" itself means "abode of clouds".

NOTE

• Meghalaya's living root bridges and caves are famous; the state's capital is Shillong. Contrast: the driest region of India is western Rajasthan (Jaisalmer area).

question: How many countries share their land borders with India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Seven.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Seven countries share land borders with India: Pakistan, Afghanistan, China, Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh and Myanmar. (भारत की स्थल सीमा से लगे 7 देश)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• India's total land frontier is about 15,106.7 km; the longest land border is with Bangladesh (about 4,096.7 km) and the shortest with Afghanistan (106 km, along PoK).

• Border lines: Radcliffe Line (India–Pakistan/Bangladesh), McMahon Line (India–China, eastern sector), Line of Actual Control (LAC) and Line of Control (LoC).

• India's maritime neighbours include Sri Lanka and Maldives (separated by sea, no land border); Sri Lanka is separated by the Palk Strait and Gulf of Mannar.

NOTE

• India has a coastline of about 7,516.6 km (mainland 6,100 km); 17 states/UTs touch international land borders — Bangladesh borders the maximum number of Indian states (5).
